summary: Nine dead items remain (a tenth, envelope.py's follow_up docstring, was fixed by the concurrent agent at 19:31 while this was being written), and one of them is not merely dead but actively destructive. THE HEADLINE: envelope.validate_event no longer accepts follow_up -- it was dropped from the writable-field set -- while WORLD_SYSTEM still carries a six-line paragraph teaching the model to emit it (world_mind.py:209-215). A world response that obeys the prompt is now rejected outright with EnvelopeError('event has fields the model may not write: [follow_up]') -- verified by executing it -- costing two calls and committing nothing. This is worse than the defect class you asked about: the prompt does not merely shape the model's answer for nothing, it shapes it into a rejection. THE SECOND REAL ONE: evaluation/verify_run.py:20 hard-codes a five-value WAKE_PROVENANCE set that is wrong in both directions -- three of its values (observed_event, known_deadline, action_completion) are provenances the runtime deliberately deleted and can never emit, and it is MISSING own_act_finished, which the runtime schedules at trajectory.py:496, so every run containing an own_act_finished wake now fails acceptance with 'a wake has provenance own_act_finished'. That is the fourth and fifth surviving instance of the exact wake-provenance defect that has already bitten twice. The remaining seven are small and mechanical: two unused imports in adapter.py, one unused function parameter in trace.py, three computed-then-discarded duration keys in envelope.py ('span', 'delta', and validate_wakes' 'delta' -- all three recomputed downstream from the original text), and one stale constant reference in SEMANTIC_RUNTIME_REPORT.md. Trace kinds are now clean: all 21 emitted kinds are consumed, and nothing is consumed that is not emitted -- that was not true 20 minutes ago. Separately: 13 categories of ledger key, view key and parsed key are written and never read back. All are correct by design (the ledger IS the artifact) and are catalogued under trace_only so a deletion pass does not mistake unreadness for deadness -- in particular, replay._projection compares the entire build_view dict field-by-field, so pruning any view key silently weakens what replay verifies.

live_but_suspicious.name: attempt_id
live_but_suspicious.file:line: written at trajectory.py OP_ATTEMPT site and journal.py:68; READ at replay.py:93 and replay.py:104
live_but_suspicious.verdict: LIVE -- but by exactly one reader, and not during the run.
live_but_suspicious.detail: You asked directly whether attempt_id is ever read. It is, once: replay.check_ledger_integrity builds by_attempt = {attempt_id: actor} from semantic.attempt records and uses it to decide whether an own_doing observation is legal ('the own-doing exemption is tied to a real attempt by that person, not to a free-text string: four words used to switch off the only ledger rule guarding the information boundary'). A mismatch appends a ledger_integrity problem, forcing replay exact=False, which evaluation/verify_run.py turns into a run failure -- so it does change output. During the run itself it is only carried: world_step takes it, puts it in the K_EVENT payload, journal.commit stores it. Nothing at commit time or judgment time consults it. tests/test_runtime_completion.py:292-296 is the only other reader and it asserts. So the stated purpose -- 'nothing bound a committed consequence to the attempt it came from, so a YES could rest on a chain whose decisive step was never taken by anybody' -- is enforced only after the fact, by the replay verifier, and never by the judge.

live_but_suspicious.name: intends_after_cutoff
live_but_suspicious.file:line: trajectory.py -- one writer (inside _schedule_wake), one reader (the reached_horizon assignment)
live_but_suspicious.verdict: LIVE, but written from one of the two places that arguably should both write it.
live_but_suspicious.detail: It is set only when a WAKE falls past the cutoff. The symmetric case -- a world-proposed EVENT whose due time falls past the cutoff -- emits note('event_beyond_cutoff') and does NOT set the flag. Both are 'the world has said what the future holds and none of it lands before the deadline', which is the exact justification the comment above the flag gives for its existence. As written, a run whose only known future is a beyond-cutoff event reports incomplete_empty_queue rather than an honest cutoff, and therefore cannot answer NO. Not dead; the asymmetry looks unintended.

live_but_suspicious.detail: news and news_at_turn gate the same-instant re-consultation guard and _has_learned_something. arrivals_asked deduplicates the pending_progression question per (actor, event). last_progression is the (instant, record size, item ids) triple that makes 'the same question' precise -- and deliberately includes the instant, so a later ask is a different question. reached_horizon is the sole input to the empty-queue-vs-honest-cutoff decision. did_it and self_act_of are genuinely distinct and both read: did_it grants the author observation of their OWN event only, self_act_of suppresses news and hands the turn back down the whole consequence chain. prompt_fields_consumed_by_nothing.instruction_text: "follow_up" is true when this event leaves ONE unresolved thing for the world to work out next -- something is in transit, something is underway, something will arrive. It is false when the event is finished in itself: somebody has put a thing down, an arrival has arrived, a person now has the situation in front of them. When it is false, nothing further is asked and the next thing to happen is somebody's decision or a later scheduled event.
prompt_fields_consumed_by_nothing.what_the_runtime_does_with_it: Nothing, and now worse than nothing. No branch has read envelope['follow_up'] since the transport chain was deleted. As of the current tree, validate_event REJECTS any response carrying it -- verified by execution. So the six-line paragraph makes the model compute a field whose presence causes the entire response to be thrown away and retried, spending two calls and committing nothing. Every claim the paragraph makes about consequences ('when it is false, nothing further is asked') is also false: what follows an event is decided by the observed/for state and by self_act_of, not by this flag.

prompt_fields_consumed_by_nothing.instruction_text: Say WHAT you will revisit and why that time means something. Never ask to "reconsider later" or to check again in general -- that is not a plan, and it will be refused. ... and -- if this is not finished for you -- when will you next come back to it, and why then? If you genuinely expect to think about this again, say so in "next_wake"; nothing else will bring it back to you.
prompt_fields_consumed_by_nothing.what_the_runtime_does_with_it: The 'after' is fully consumed -- it schedules the wake. The reason's CONTENT is not. validate_next_wake enforces only non-emptiness and parseability; _schedule_wake stores it in the K_WAKE payload and emits it to grounded_wakes.jsonl. The single place a wake reason is read back is the world_process branch, and actor wakes never carry that provenance. So the prompt spends three sentences demanding a specific, grounded, non-generic reason, the validator refuses a vague one, and when the wake fires the reason is discarded and the actor sees only 'time has passed and you are looking at your situation again'.
prompt_fields_consumed_by_nothing.severity: MEDIUM -- defensible as an anti-polling forcing function (demanding a real reason is what stops next_wake becoming a timer), indefensible if read as 'the runtime uses this'. envelope.py:219-224 is honest about it for world wakes ('its reason is recorded for tracing and is shown to no one'); the actor prompt is not.
